newsitem.title: CANADA: Saskatchewan sees C$24.1 mln surplus in 1997/98.
newsitem.headline: Saskatchewan sees C$24.1 mln surplus in 1997/98.

text.p: The Canadian province of Saskatchewan on Thursday said its budget for fiscal 1997/98 ending March 31 projects a surplus of C$24.1 million.
It was the fourth straight balanced budget from Saskatchewan Finance Minister Janice MacKinnon.
Saskatchewan's provincial sales tax will be cut to seven percent from nine at 2400 CST Thursday, 0600 GMT on Friday.
"These are the rewards of sound, careful management of the public purse. Our economy is strong and growing, our fiscal position is strong and we're paying down the public debt," MacKinnon said.
Revenues were forecast at C$5.07 billion in fiscal 1997/98 compared to C$5.48 billion in the current year, budget documents showed.
Operating expenses were projected at C$4.28 billion in 1997/98 compared to C$4.32 billion.
The budget surplus was forecast at C$24.1 million in 1997/98 compared to C$368.9 million in the current year.
MacKinnon's C$180 million sales tax reduction follows prior cuts to personal and business income taxes.
She announced new investments in roads, health, education and social programs.

Three other tax cuts announced by MacKinnon include: --a sales tax rebate on building materials and equipment for livestock and horticultural activities to assist in tripling Saskatchewan's hog production by 2005. --an extension of the Manufacturing and Processing Investment Tax Credit to include taxable used equipment. --a new sales tax exemption on some medical devices.
